fields.rationale: Wishbone B4 does NOT define a JTAG / scan / BIST / MBIST / debug architecture. There is no dedicated debug interface in the protocol. Debug visibility, if any, must be added by the integrator outside this spec (e.g. SignalTap on an FPGA, JTAG/CoreSight on an ASIC SoC). The Wishbone goal is explicitly that the architecture be 'independent of FPGA and ASIC test methodologies' (1.1 WISHBONE Features).

spec_provided_observability.name: [ACK_I] normal termination
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Indicates normal end of a bus cycle; observable by the MASTER (and any monitoring logic on the INTERCON).

spec_provided_observability.name: [ERR_I] error termination
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Indicates abnormal cycle termination (e.g. parity fault, address-decode error, watchdog timeout). Useful for fault monitoring.

spec_provided_observability.name: [RTY_I] retry termination
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Indicates the SLAVE is temporarily busy; the MASTER must retry the cycle later. Useful for shared resources / bridges.

spec_provided_observability.name: Tag types ([TGA_O()], [TGD_O()], [TGD_I()], [TGC_O()], [TGC_I()])
spec_provided_observability.purpose: User-defined tags for parity, error correction, interrupt vectors, cache control hints, etc. The spec fixes their timing (qualified with [STB_O] or [CYC_O] per Table 3-1); their semantics are user-defined and MUST be documented in the WISHBONE DATASHEET (RULE 3.70).

spec_provided_observability.name: [LOCK_O] / [LOCK_I]
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Indicates an indivisible (uninterruptible) bus cycle. Useful for atomic semaphore operations and for debug observation of arbitration ownership.

interconnect_observability: INTERCON-level watchdog timers (RECOMMENDATION 3.10) — monitor MASTER [STB_O] and inject [ERR_I] or [RTY_I] if a cycle exceeds a time limit; can also disconnect the misbehaving interface.
INTERCON-level scoreboarding — observe each phase's [ADR_O] + [STB_O] + termination signal to track outstanding transactions, useful for protocol-conformance verification.

optional_features_per_supplier.ERR_RTY_optionality: PERMISSION 3.20 / 3.25 — MASTER and SLAVE interfaces MAY be designed to support [ERR_I]/[ERR_O] and [RTY_I]/[RTY_O]; if supported, the IP supplier defines how the cycle is responded to and retried (RULE 2.15 items 4, 5).
optional_features_per_supplier.Tag_semantics: Each user-defined tag is assigned a TAG TYPE per Table 3-1 (TGA_O/I, TGD_I, TGD_O, TGC_O/I) and the IP supplier defines the tag's semantics in the WISHBONE DATASHEET (RULE 3.70 + RULE 2.15 item 6).
optional_features_per_supplier.LOCK_optionality: [LOCK_O]/[LOCK_I] is optional; only required when atomic / uninterruptible transfers are needed.
optional_features_per_supplier.Registered_Feedback_optionality: Chapter 4 cycles are an OPTIONAL extension (PERMISSION 4.00). All Registered Feedback compatible cores MUST also support Classic cycles (RULE 4.00). Backwards compatible — if either side does not support Registered Feedback, the cycle terminates as a Classic cycle.

fields.spec_recommended_design_for_test_hints: Watchdog timer in INTERCON (RECOMMENDATION 3.10) is the main built-in design-for-test/debug hint. The spec also recommends registered MASTER outputs on [STB_O]/[CYC_O] (RECOMMENDATION 3.15) which simplifies timing closure and helps STA-based debug.

evidence.quote: Independent of FPGA and ASIC test methodologies. Seamless design progression between FPGA prototypes and ASIC production chips.

If a MASTER supports the optional [ERR_I] signal, then the WISHBONE DATASHEET MUST describe how it reacts in response to the signal. If a SLAVE supports the optional [ERR_O] signal, then the WISHBONE DATASHEET MUST describe the conditions under which the signal is generated. The same applies for [RTY_I] / [RTY_O]. All interfaces that support tag signals MUST describe the name, TAG TYPE and operation of the tag in the WISHBONE DATASHEET.

The lock output [LOCK_O] when asserted, indicates that the current bus cycle is uninterruptible. Lock is asserted to request complete ownership of the bus. Once the transfer has started, the INTERCON does not grant the bus to any other MASTER, until the current MASTER negates [LOCK_O] or [CYC_O].

The error input [ERR_I] indicates an abnormal cycle termination. The source of the error, and the response generated by the MASTER is defined by the IP core supplier. The retry input [RTY_I] indicates that the interface is not ready to accept or send data, and that the cycle should be retried. When and how the cycle is retried is defined by the IP core supplier.

Design INTERCON modules to prevent deadlock conditions. One solution to this problem is to include a watchdog timer function that monitors the MASTER's [STB_O] signal, and asserts [ERR_I] or [RTY_I] if the cycle exceeds some pre-defined time limit. INTERCON modules can also be designed to disconnect interfaces from the WISHBONE bus if they constantly generate bus errors and/or watchdog time-outs.

All tag signals MUST conform to a set of guidelines known as TAG TYPEs. Table 3-1 lists all of the defined TAG TYPEs along with their associated data set and signal waveform. When a tag is added to an interface it is assigned a TAG TYPE from the table.
